The proposed models are de- signed to be integrated as a dedicated package within the MBL as "MotorDrive". This inte- gration will enhance the library’s capability to model grid-interactive building systems, en- ablingresearchersandpractitionerstoevaluateenergyperformance,analyzegridresponsive- ness, and develop advanced control strategies with ease. The proposed model (Figure 3.9) receives voltage and frequency signals from the power system, and the user can provide set points for the chiller, heat pump, and pump as required. The case study is designed to model the interac- tion of these systems with the power grid, focusing on operational behavior under varying electricalgridconditions. To analyze the influence of the electrical grid on various systems, a series of case studies were conducted, subjecting an induction machine (CEAIM) (Figure 3.10), pump (CEAIM- pump) (Figure 3.11), chiller (CEAIM-Chiller) (Figure 3.12) and heat pump (CEAIM-Heat Pump) (Figure 3.13) to sudden changes in load voltage. This scenario helps to evaluate the transient and steady-state behavior, focusing on key aspects such as voltage stability, electromagnetictorquefluctuations,andsystem-specificresponses,includingmassflowrate heatingandcoolingperformance.
